t.1.151.1: Then, when the night had passed, the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena took the food and went to the place where that man-eater was.
t.1.151.2: Having reached the forest of that Rākṣasa, the mighty Pāṇḍava then called him by name, while eating that food himself.
t.1.151.3: Then that Rākṣasa, having heard those words of Bhīmasena, came, greatly enraged, to where Bhīma was stationed.
t.1.151.4: Huge of body and tremendous in speed, as though splitting the earth asunder, he came on, knitting his brows into a three-furrowed frown and biting down on his lip.
t.1.151.5: Seeing Bhīmasena eating the food, the rākṣasa, enraged, opened wide his eyes and spoke these words.
t.1.151.6: Who is this fool who, while I look on, eats this food that was prepared for me, wishing to go to the abode of Yama?
t.1.151.7: But Bhīmasena, hearing that, as if laughing, O Bhārata, paid no heed to the Rākṣasa and went on eating, his face turned away.
t.1.151.8: Then the man-eater, letting out a terrifying roar and raising both his hands, rushed at Bhīmasena, eager to kill him.
t.1.151.10: But the Rākṣasa, filled with fury, standing behind him, struck the back of Kuntī's son with both his hands.
t.1.151.9: Even so, disregarding him and not looking at the rākṣasa, Vṛkodara, the Pāṇḍava, slayer of enemy heroes, simply went on eating the food.
t.1.151.12: Then the mighty Rākṣasa, enraged once more, seized a tree and, intending to strike Bhīma, rushed at him again.
t.1.151.11: Though struck hard in this way with both hands by the mighty one, Bhīma did not even glance at the Rākṣasa; he simply went on eating.
t.1.151.14: That tree, hurled by the enraged one, the mighty Bhīma caught with his left hand, as if laughing, O Bhārata.
t.1.151.13: Then Bhīma, bull among men, having slowly eaten that food and sipped water, stood ready for battle, thrilled, the mighty one.
t.1.151.16: Then, great king, there arose a great tree-fight between Baka and the Pāṇḍava, terrible in form and destructive of the trees.
t.1.151.15: Then the mighty one, again raising up trees of many kinds, hurled them at Bhīmasena, and Bhīma the Pāṇḍava hurled them back at him.
t.1.151.17: But Baka, having proclaimed his name, rushed at the Pāṇḍava and seized mighty Bhīmasena with both his arms.
t.1.151.18: Bhīmasena too, the mighty-armed and powerful one, clasped that rākṣasa in his arms and dragged him about by force as he writhed with great vehemence.
t.1.151.19: Being dragged by Bhīma and dragging the Pāṇḍava in turn, the man-eater was overcome by intense exhaustion.
t.1.151.20: Through the great force of those two, the earth trembled, and then they pulverized the huge-bodied trees.
t.1.151.21: But seeing that rākṣasa weakening, O bull of the Bharatas, Vṛkodara crushed him against the ground and struck him with both his hands.
t.1.151.22: Then, pressing down his back with his knee as if with great force, he seized his neck with his right arm.
t.1.151.24: Then, O lord of the people, blood gushed forth from the mouth of that terrible Rākṣasa as he was being broken by Bhīma.
t.1.151.23: And with his left hand the Pāṇḍava seized him by the garment at the waist and bent that rākṣasa double, while it bellowed terrible roars.
